Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Niger has the Politique de Développement du Numérique 2023-2032 and updated Telecommunications Code (2018). The legal framework for e-transactions and data sharing is under development but no specific cross-government data sharing law found. AFD/Expertise France noted improving the legal framework as an objective.

revised_comments: Niger does not yet have a dedicated law establishing cross-government data-sharing authority or governing a national data exchange system, though several adjacent legal instruments exist. These include the 2018 Telecommunications Code, the 2019 law on electronic transactions, and the personal data protection law (Law n°2022-59 of December 2022, amended by Law n°2023-31 of July 2023), which created the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (HAPDP) and regulates data interconnection and cross-border transfer. The Politique de Développement du Numérique 2023-2032 references strengthening the legal and institutional framework for digital governance, and a successor National Digital Policy is under preparation, but no specific data exchange or interoperability law has been enacted. Government communications as recently as April 2026 continue to flag gaps in interoperability between civil registration and identification systems, with legal reforms still in draft, indicating the enabling legislation remains under development.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Niger adopted a Politique de Développement du Numérique 2023-2032 which mentions digitalization of public administration. The Niger 2.0 strategy (2020) covered e-government services. However, neither document constitutes a comprehensive data exchange/interoperability strategy. ANSI (Agence Nationale pour la Société de l'Information) coordinates digital government.

Further searches found that Niger is now finalising a successor National Digital Policy (PNDN 2026-2035) and sectoral plan (PSDN 2026-2030), validated at a workshop on 11 March 2026, which include an axis on strengthening digital-sector governance and e-government but, like its predecessors, is a broad digital strategy rather than a dedicated data exchange/interoperability strategy. revised_comments: Niger has no standalone strategy dedicated to government data exchange and interoperability; the topic is addressed only within broader digital transformation policy. The Politique de Développement du Numérique 2023-2032 and its predecessor, the Niger 2.0 strategy (2020), reference digitalisation of public administration and e-government services but do not set out a specific data exchange or interoperability framework. As of March 2026 the government is validating a successor National Digital Policy (PNDN 2026-2035) alongside a sectoral plan (PSDN 2026-2030), which include an axis on strengthening digital governance and advancing e-government but again fall short of a comprehensive, dedicated interoperability strategy. ANSI, and increasingly the newer Agence de Développement Numérique, coordinate cross-ministerial digitalisation and interoperability initiatives (e.g. land administration, civil registration) on an administrative rather than strategic-document basis.
